content: The LARGE glycosyltransferase-like protein, also known as LARGE1, is an enzyme in humans encoded by the LARGE gene. This gene is one of the largest in the human genome and belongs to the N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase gene family. The precise function of the LARGE protein, which is localized to the Golgi apparatus, remains unclear. However, it encodes a glycosyltransferase enzyme that is involved in the glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan. This process may contribute to the synthesis of sugar chains in glycoproteins and glycosphingolipids. Additionally, the enzyme may play a role in the addition of repeated disaccharide units. Mutations in the LARGE gene are known to cause MDC1D, a distinct form of congenital muscular dystrophy characterized by severe mental retardation and abnormal glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan. Alternative splicing of this gene results in two transcript variants that encode the same protein. The LARGE protein may also be implicated in tumor-specific genomic rearrangements. Mutations in this gene could contribute to the development and progression of meningioma by altering the composition of gangliosides and other glycosylated molecules in tumor cells.
